headline: Highest risk is data leakage: Rasa can egress to allowlisted APIs while mem0 is a memory store with no documented isolation, creating a plausible shared-data path; other risks are lower and mostly undocumented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, but Rasa exposes multiple messaging APIs and mem0 is a knowledge-management component that may ingest external text. Without a documented bridge, prompt injection is only plausible via unusual copy/paste or integration glue, so the blast radius is limited and uncertainty keeps this above none.
conditions: IF an operator wires Rasa message text into mem0 prompts or memory writes
IF a shared clipboard, queue, or filesystem bridge is added between the agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate channels with no automatic text forwarding
Disable any copy/paste workflow that moves raw bot output into mem0
Add a manual review step before mem0 ingests Rasa-generated content
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all cross-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: Rasa has allowlisted network egress and handles text/voice, while mem0 is a memory system with no isolation or data-class limits shown. A shared workspace or integration could move sensitive conversation content from mem0 into Rasa outputs or upstream APIs in default deployments, so leakage is plausible even though direct evidence is absent.
conditions: IF mem0 stores user conversation history that is later surfaced to Rasa
IF Rasa forwards conversation text to any allowlisted third-party API
IF both agents are connected to the same workspace or message bus
mitigations: Restrict Rasa connectors to non-sensitive channels only
Redact memory entries before they are exposed to Rasa
Separate storage for mem0 and Rasa with distinct credentials
Audit outbound API destinations in Rasa before deployment
requires-engineering: enforce field-level data-loss prevention between the agents

C_capability_conflict.rationale: mem0 shows no write or network surface beyond none, while Rasa supports allowlisted egress and multiple external chat APIs. The profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same mutable resource, so direct conflict is not established; uncertainty remains because the shared orchestrator is undocumented.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same database, filesystem, or bot channel
IF an orchestrator lets them mutate the same conversation state without locking
mitigations: Assign separate storage locations and credentials
Avoid concurrent writes to shared bot state
Serialize updates through one coordinator
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Rasa is a customer-support bot that can act on dialogue, and mem0 is a memory layer whose outputs may be treated as context. If Rasa consumes mem0 content without verification, stale or incorrect memory can cascade into user-facing responses or actions; the profiles do not show a built-in validation step, so the pathway is plausible in default integrations.
conditions: IF Rasa uses mem0 output as authoritative conversation context
IF no verification or human review occurs before Rasa responds
mitigations: Insert a validation step before Rasa consumes memory
Limit mem0 to retrieval-only hints, not instructions
Flag low-confidence memories for manual review
Log source provenance for every memory item
requires-engineering: add policy checks before downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, but Rasa touches text and voice and can send data through external messaging APIs, while mem0 is a memory store with no residency or retention controls documented. A compliance mismatch is possible if regulated conversation data is stored in mem0 and then routed through Rasa connectors, but the profiles do not prove a specific jurisdictional breach.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is stored in mem0 and routed through Rasa connectors
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two systems
mitigations: Document retention rules for both agents
Exclude regulated data from Rasa channels
Purge memory entries on deletion requests
Review connector destinations for residency constraints
requires-engineering: align DPA and retention controls across both systems
